summary: A Tesla Model S driving on Autopilot crashed into a white tractor-trailer crossing a Florida highway, killing its driver. The car's sensors did not distinguish the truck from the bright sky, and the driver may have been watching a movie.
technical_summary: Tesla's Autopilot driver-assistance system failed to detect a white trailer crossing the road against a bright sky and did not brake. The driver was reportedly not attending to the road, showing the combined effect of perception failure and over-reliance on partial automation.

technology.quote: The Tesla driver killed in the first known fatal crash involving a self-driving car

failure_mode.quote: the car’s sensor system, against a bright spring sky, failed to distinguish a large white 18-wheel truck and trailer crossing the highway
may have been watching a Harry Potter movie at the time of the collision

harm_type.quote: The Tesla driver killed in the first known fatal crash involving a self-driving car

severity.quote: The Tesla driver killed in the first known fatal crash involving a self-driving car

notes: Movie-watching is a witness claim; Tesla said both driver and system failed to notice the trailer.

summary: Target reportedly used shoppers' purchase histories to predict pregnancy and send maternity coupons, in a widely told story of a teenager's family learning of her pregnancy from the mailers. Critics doubt the anecdote is true.
technical_summary: Target built a model that scores each shopper's likelihood of pregnancy and estimated due date from purchases of about 25 products tied to an individual guest ID, then timed targeted coupons. The system inferred sensitive health status without customer knowledge or consent.

technology.quote: he was able to identify about 25 products that, when analyzed together, allowed him to assign each shopper a “pregnancy prediction” score

failure_mode.quote: has figured out how to data-mine its way into your womb, to figure out whether you have a baby on the way

affected_population.quote: Target assigns every customer a Guest ID number, tied to their credit card, name, or email address

notes: The specific family anecdote is disputed as probably untrue; the existence of the prediction model is reported by the NYT.

summary: Facebook's automated moderation removed posts and restricted users who shared an article containing an 1890s photograph of Aboriginal men in chains, wrongly flagging it as nudity. Facebook later apologized and called it an error.
technical_summary: An automated nudity classifier flagged a historical photo documenting slavery in Australia and blocked reposts of a news link, with some users banned for up to 30 days. Review capacity was reduced during the pandemic, and users reported no clear way to appeal.

sector.quote: Facebook has removed a photo of aboriginal men used to prove racism in Australia, after claiming the photo included nudity

technology.quote: the removal was the result of an automated process and was an error

failure_mode.quote: the removal was the result of an automated process and was an error
it immediately blocked the post, gave me no chance to appeal or dispute

notes: Suppression of historical evidence about colonial violence is the contextual harm.

summary: Japanese police arrested a man who used AI to reconstruct the pixelated parts of adult videos and sold the results online, in the country's first criminal case involving AI-manipulated content. He pleaded guilty to copyright and obscenity charges.
technical_summary: Machine-learning software, using methods similar to deepfake face swaps, reconstructed mosaic-censored regions from a large dataset of uncensored nude images. The altered videos were sold online, violating Japan's obscenity law and the content owners' copyright; the performers' consent was not addressed in the charges.
deployers: Individual website operator in Hyogo, Japan

sector.quote: lifted images of porn stars from Japanese adult videos and doctored them

technology.quote: using artificial intelligence to effectively unblur pixelated porn videos

failure_mode.quote: pleaded guilty to charges of copyright violation and displaying obscene images and said he did it for money

harm_type.quote: pleaded guilty to charges of copyright violation and displaying obscene images and said he did it for money

notes: Performers' privacy and consent were not part of the charges; harm to them is not documented.

summary: A Stanford study found that speech recognition tools from five major tech companies made roughly twice as many transcription errors for Black speakers as for white speakers.
technical_summary: Commercial automatic speech recognition systems from Amazon, Apple, Google, IBM and Microsoft showed an average word error rate of 0.35 for Black speakers versus 0.19 for white speakers. Researchers traced the gap to the acoustic models, likely reflecting training data lacking African American Vernacular English.

technology.quote: we demonstrate large racial disparities in the performance of five popular commercial ASR systems

failure_mode.quote: Speech recognition systems have more trouble understanding black users’ voices than those of white users

lifecycle_stage.quote: the racial gap is likely the product of bias in the datasets that train the system

affected_population.quote: Speech recognition systems have more trouble understanding black users’ voices than those of white users

notes: Study tested the companies' cloud ASR tools, not necessarily those inside consumer assistants.

summary: Volvo's self-driving test SUVs lost function in extreme cold in northern Sweden when snow and ice caked on their radar sensors, leaving the vehicles effectively blind until engineers relocated the sensors.
technical_summary: Ice and snow accumulating on exposed radar sensors degraded or blocked perception for Volvo's autonomous XC90 during winter testing. Engineers resolved it by relocating the radar behind the windshield where wipers can clear it, illustrating sensor limitations in adverse weather.

technology.quote: Volvo Cars’ self-driving XC90 sport-utility vehicle met its match: frozen flakes that caked on radar sensors essential to reading the road

failure_mode.quote: Volvo Cars’ self-driving XC90 sport-utility vehicle met its match: frozen flakes that caked on radar sensors essential to reading the road

notes: Test-phase limitation; no injury or crash reported.

summary: After a system update, a delivery company's customer service chatbot swore at a customer and wrote poems criticizing the company when prompted. The post went viral and the company disabled the AI part of the chatbot.
technical_summary: A customer-facing AI chatbot, likely a large language model, behaved unexpectedly after an update and could be easily prompted to produce profanity and disparage the company. The operator disabled the AI element, indicating weak output guardrails and inadequate pre-release testing.

technology.quote: uses artificial intelligence (AI) in its online chat to answer queries, in addition to human operators

failure_mode.quote: DPD has disabled part of its online support chatbot after it swore at a customer
But a new update caused it to behave unexpectedly, including swearing and criticising the company.
The chatbot was easily convinced to swear at the customer - pixelation added

notes: The customer deliberately prompted the bot, but the company attributed the issue to a system update error.

summary: Reporting found TikTok's For You feed pushed misogynistic videos by an online personality to young male users, helped by coordinated efforts to game the algorithm, despite platform rules banning such content.
technical_summary: TikTok's recommendation algorithm surfaced misogynistic content to a test teen account after minimal engagement. Followers of the creator also coordinated copycat accounts and clip flooding to manipulate engagement signals, exploiting engagement-driven ranking while moderation enforcement of misogyny rules was weak.

technology.quote: TikTok is promoting misogynistic content to young people despite claiming to ban it

failure_mode.quote: a “blatant attempt to manipulate the algorithm” and artificially boost his content

notes: Both algorithmic amplification and deliberate manipulation by followers are described; offline harm is asserted by advocates, not documented.

summary: Tesla's heavily automated Model 3 factory failed to hit production targets, with analysts and the CEO attributing the shortfall to over-automation. Workers had to hand-assemble parts to catch up.
technical_summary: Tesla tried to automate final assembly and battery pack production with large numbers of robots. The automated lines were too complex and brittle to scale, causing Model 3 output to fall far below targets until humans were brought in for tasks the robots could not handle reliably.

technology.quote: Tesla has tried to hyper-automate final assembly.

failure_mode.quote: So far, it has failed to manufacture even half that number.

notes: Harm is corporate production shortfall; incident date and attribution rely on analyst commentary.

summary: Brand safety technology vendors marketed advanced AI but were reportedly blocking ads using simple keyword lists, including on mainstream news pages mentioning coronavirus, which diverted ad money to lower quality sites.
technical_summary: Brand safety tools claimed to use AI and machine learning but relied on blunt keyword blocklists without context understanding. They blocked ads on legitimate news pages containing words such as covid-19, shifting advertising spend away from news publishers and toward lower quality sites.

sector.quote: ads on the front pages of New York Times and Wall Street Journal were blocked and replaced by “cloud ads”

technology.quote: it was painfully clear the brand safety technology was blocking ads based on simple keyword lists

failure_mode.quote: it was painfully clear the brand safety technology was blocking ads based on simple keyword lists

harm_type.quote: The result of this blocking is that more ads and dollars flow to lower quality sites in programmatic channels

notes: Also involves allegedly overstated AI claims by vendors.

summary: A New Zealand supermarket's AI meal-planner app suggested recipes that would create toxic chlorine gas and other dangerous mixtures when users entered household items. The company said users misused the tool and promised tighter controls.
technical_summary: A generative meal-planning bot accepted non-food household items as ingredients and produced cheerful recipes for hazardous combinations, including chlorine gas, without adequate input validation or safety filtering. The app warned that recipes were not reviewed by a human.

failure_mode.quote: One recipe it dubbed “aromatic water mix” would create chlorine gas.
a small minority have tried to use the tool inappropriately and not for its intended purpose

affected_population.quote: recommending customers recipes for deadly chlorine gas

notes: No injuries reported; users deliberately entered unusual items.

summary: A Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot hit a pickup truck on a California freeway at about 60 mph, killing a 15-year-old passenger. Vehicle data showed neither Autopilot nor the driver slowed until a fraction of a second before impact.
technical_summary: Tesla Autopilot, a partial-automation driver-assistance system, did not detect or brake for a vehicle that had moved into its lane and the driver also did not react in time. Regulators have opened investigations into multiple Autopilot crashes involving failure to detect obstacles.

failure_mode.quote: At least three Tesla drivers have died since 2016 in crashes in which Autopilot was engaged and failed to detect obstacles in the road.
nor the driver slowed the vehicle until a fraction of a second before the crash

harm_type.quote: was thrown from the Ford and died, according to a police report

severity.quote: was thrown from the Ford and died, according to a police report

notes: Lawsuit pending; the passenger was reportedly unbelted. Driver and system both implicated.
